- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

31	func newHTTPClient() *http.Client {
32		transport := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport).Clone()
33		transport.Proxy = nil
34		transport.DialContext = secureDialContext

36		return &http.Client{

46				return nil

51	func secureDialContext(ctx context.Context, network, address string) (net.Conn, error) {
52		host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(address)
53		if err != nil {
54			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "invalid address")
55		}
56	
57		ips, err := resolveAllowedIPs(ctx, host)
58		if err != nil {
59			return nil, err
60		}
61	
62		var dialErr error
63		for _, ip := range ips {
64			conn, err := dialContext(ctx, network, net.JoinHostPort(ip.String(), port))
65			if err == nil {
66				return conn, nil
67			}
68			dialErr = err
69		}
70		return nil, dialErr
71	}

73	func resolveAllowedIPs(ctx context.Context, host string) ([]net.IP, error) {
74		if ip := net.ParseIP(host); ip != nil {
75			if isInternalIP(ip) {
76				return nil, errors.Wrap(ErrInternalIP, ip.String())
77			}
78			return []net.IP{ip}, nil
79		}
80	
81		addrs, err := lookupIPAddr(ctx, host)
82		if err != nil {
83			return nil, errors.Errorf("failed to resolve hostname: %v", err)
84		}
85	
86		ips := make([]net.IP, 0, len(addrs))
87		for _, addr := range addrs {
88			ip := addr.IP
89			if ip == nil {
90				continue
91			}
92			if isInternalIP(ip) {
93				return nil, errors.Wrapf(ErrInternalIP, "host=%s, ip=%s", host, ip.String())
94			}
95			ips = append(ips, ip)
96		}
97		if len(ips) == 0 {
98			return nil, errors.New("hostname resolved to no addresses")
99		}
100	
101		return ips, nil
102	}

104	func isInternalIP(ip net.IP) bool {
105		return ip.IsLoopback() || ip.IsPrivate() || ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() || ip.IsUnspecified()

108	func validateURL(urlStr string) error {
109		u, err := url.Parse(urlStr)
110		if err != nil {
111			return errors.New("invalid URL format")
112		}
113	
114		if u.Scheme != "http" && u.Scheme != "https" {
115			return errors.New("only http/https protocols are allowed")
116		}
117	
118		host := u.Hostname()
119		if host == "" {
120			return errors.New("empty hostname")
121		}
122	
123		if ip := net.ParseIP(host); ip != nil && isInternalIP(ip) {
124			return errors.Wrap(ErrInternalIP, ip.String())
125		}
126	
127		return nil
128	}

160	func extractHTMLMeta(resp io.Reader) *HTMLMeta {
161		tokenizer := html.NewTokenizer(resp)
162		htmlMeta := new(HTMLMeta)
163	
164		for {
165			tokenType := tokenizer.Next()
166			if tokenType == html.ErrorToken {
167				break
168			} else if tokenType == html.StartTagToken || tokenType == html.SelfClosingTagToken {
169				token := tokenizer.Token()
170				if token.DataAtom == atom.Body {
171					break
172				}
173	
174				if token.DataAtom == atom.Title {
175					tokenizer.Next()
176					token := tokenizer.Token()
177					htmlMeta.Title = token.Data
178				} else if token.DataAtom == atom.Meta {
179					ogTitle, ok := extractMetaProperty(token, "og:title")
180					if ok {
181						htmlMeta.Title = ogTitle
182					}
183	
184					ogDescription, ok := extractMetaProperty(token, "og:description")
185					if ok {
186						htmlMeta.Description = ogDescription
187					}
188	
189					ogImage, ok := extractMetaProperty(token, "og:image")
190					if ok {
191						htmlMeta.Image = ogImage
192					}
193	
194					description, ok := extractMetaProperty(token, "description")
195					if ok && htmlMeta.Description == "" {
196						htmlMeta.Description = description
197					}
198				}
199			}
200		}
201	
202		return htmlMeta
203	}

205	func extractMetaProperty(token html.Token, prop string) (content string, ok bool) {
206		content, ok = "", false
207		for _, attr := range token.Attr {
208			if (attr.Key == "property" || attr.Key == "name") && strings.EqualFold(attr.Val, prop) {
209				ok = true
210			}
211			if attr.Key == "content" {
212				content = attr.Val
213			}
214		}
215		return content, ok
216	}

86	// TestPostSignsRequest verifies the end-to-end Standard Webhooks signature so a
87	// receiver following the documented verification recipe will accept our requests.
88	func TestPostSignsRequest(t *testing.T) {
89		// httptest listens on 127.0.0.1, which the SSRF guard blocks by default.
90		prev := AllowPrivateIPs
91		AllowPrivateIPs = true
92		defer func() { AllowPrivateIPs = prev }()
93	
94		rawKey := []byte("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef")
95		cases := []struct {
96			name   string
97			secret string
98			key    []byte
99		}{
100			{name: "plain secret", secret: "plain-secret-value", key: []byte("plain-secret-value")},
101			{name: "whsec_ secret", secret: "whsec_" + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(rawKey), key: rawKey},
102		}
103	
104		for _, tc := range cases {
105			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
106				var gotID, gotTimestamp, gotSignature string
107				var gotBody []byte
108				server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
109					gotID = r.Header.Get("webhook-id")
110					gotTimestamp = r.Header.Get("webhook-timestamp")
111					gotSignature = r.Header.Get("webhook-signature")
112					gotBody, _ = io.ReadAll(r.Body)
113					_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"code":0}`))
114				}))
115				defer server.Close()
116	
117				err := Post(&WebhookRequestPayload{
118					URL:           server.URL,
119					ActivityType:  "memos.memo.created",
120					Creator:       "users/1",
121					SigningSecret: tc.secret,
122				})
123				require.NoError(t, err)
124	
125				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotID, "msg_"), "webhook-id should be prefixed with msg_")
126				require.NotEmpty(t, gotTimestamp)
127				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotSignature, "v1,"), "signature should carry the v1 version tag")
128	
129				// Recompute the signature the way a receiver would and confirm it matches.
130				mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, tc.key)
131				mac.Write([]byte(gotID + "." + gotTimestamp + "."))
132				mac.Write(gotBody)
133				want := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
134				require.Equal(t, "v1,"+want, gotSignature)
135			})
136		}
137	}

31	func newHTTPClient() *http.Client {

51	func secureDialContext(ctx context.Context, network, address string) (net.Conn, error) {
52		host, port, err := net.SplitHostPort(address)

55		}

65			if err == nil {

67			}
68			dialErr = err

86	// TestPostSignsRequest verifies the end-to-end Standard Webhooks signature so a
87	// receiver following the documented verification recipe will accept our requests.
88	func TestPostSignsRequest(t *testing.T) {
89		// httptest listens on 127.0.0.1, which the SSRF guard blocks by default.
90		prev := AllowPrivateIPs
91		AllowPrivateIPs = true
92		defer func() { AllowPrivateIPs = prev }()
93	
94		rawKey := []byte("0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef")
95		cases := []struct {
96			name   string
97			secret string
98			key    []byte
99		}{
100			{name: "plain secret", secret: "plain-secret-value", key: []byte("plain-secret-value")},
101			{name: "whsec_ secret", secret: "whsec_" + base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(rawKey), key: rawKey},
102		}
103	
104		for _, tc := range cases {
105			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
106				var gotID, gotTimestamp, gotSignature string
107				var gotBody []byte
108				server := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
109					gotID = r.Header.Get("webhook-id")
110					gotTimestamp = r.Header.Get("webhook-timestamp")
111					gotSignature = r.Header.Get("webhook-signature")
112					gotBody, _ = io.ReadAll(r.Body)
113					_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"code":0}`))
114				}))
115				defer server.Close()
116	
117				err := Post(&WebhookRequestPayload{
118					URL:           server.URL,
119					ActivityType:  "memos.memo.created",
120					Creator:       "users/1",
121					SigningSecret: tc.secret,
122				})
123				require.NoError(t, err)
124	
125				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotID, "msg_"), "webhook-id should be prefixed with msg_")
126				require.NotEmpty(t, gotTimestamp)
127				require.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(gotSignature, "v1,"), "signature should carry the v1 version tag")
128	
129				// Recompute the signature the way a receiver would and confirm it matches.
130				mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, tc.key)
131				mac.Write([]byte(gotID + "." + gotTimestamp + "."))
132				mac.Write(gotBody)
133				want := base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
134				require.Equal(t, "v1,"+want, gotSignature)
135			})
136		}
137	}

125			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.PermissionDenied, "permission denied")

131			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to get user webhooks: %v", err)
132		}

134		// Find the webhook to update

170					if err := webhook.ValidateSigningSecret(secret); err != nil {
171						return nil, err
172					}
173					updatedWebhook.SigningSecret = secret
174				default:
175					// Ignore unsupported fields
176				}
177			}
178		} else {
179			// If no update mask is provided, update all fields
180			if request.Webhook.Url != "" {
181				trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(request.Webhook.Url)
182				if err := webhook.ValidateURL(trimmed); err != nil {
183					return nil, err
184				}
185				updatedWebhook.Url = trimmed
186			}
187			updatedWebhook.Title = request.Webhook.DisplayName
188			if request.Webhook.SigningSecret != "" {
189				secret := strings.TrimSpace(request.Webhook.SigningSecret)
190				if err := webhook.ValidateSigningSecret(secret); err != nil {
191					return nil, err
192				}
193				updatedWebhook.SigningSecret = secret
194			}
195		}
196	
197		err = s.Store.UpdateUserWebhook(ctx, userID, updatedWebhook)
198		if err != nil {
199			return nil, status.Errorf(codes.Internal, "failed to update webhook: %v", err)
200		}
201
